title: Best Linear Alternatives for Issue Tracking and Project Planning
description: Compare alternatives to Linear by workflow flexibility, developer integrations, portfolio reporting, collaboration, and administration. Choose based on the work your team must manage, not on feature counts.

alternatives.name: Jira
alternatives.description: Consider Jira when you need configurable issue workflows, backlog management, and detailed engineering reporting. Budget for administration and keep workflow rules consistent.

alternatives.name: Asana
alternatives.description: Consider Asana for cross-functional project coordination, task ownership, timeline views, and stakeholder reporting beyond software issue tracking.

alternatives.name: ClickUp
alternatives.description: Consider ClickUp when you want configurable task views and related documentation in one workspace, and can manage the added configuration.

alternatives.name: Trello
alternatives.description: Consider Trello for straightforward visual Kanban workflows where simplicity matters more than detailed dependencies or portfolio reporting.

alternatives.name: Basecamp
alternatives.description: Consider Basecamp when project communication, shared to-dos, and a simple team space matter more than advanced agile reporting.

faqs.question: What is the best alternative to Linear?
faqs.answer: It depends on the workflow. Compare Jira for configurable issue tracking, Asana for cross-functional projects, ClickUp for broad configuration, Trello for simple Kanban, and Basecamp for project communication.

faqs.question: When should an engineering team move away from Linear?
faqs.answer: Consider a change when a required workflow, report, permission model, or integration cannot be supported without recurring workarounds.

faqs.question: How should we compare alternatives?
faqs.answer: Run the same project through each candidate and compare issue management, planning, reporting, integration, permissions, migration, and total cost.

sections.title: Why Look Beyond Linear?
sections.body: Teams usually evaluate alternatives when they need different workflow customization, broader project reporting, more non-engineering use cases, or a different cost and administration model. Start by identifying the specific limitation that prompted the search. If the problem is unclear ownership or inconsistent issue writing, a new tool may not solve it. If the product genuinely lacks a required workflow, compare candidates against a short list of mandatory requirements.

sections.title: Match the Alternative to the Workflow
sections.body: Jira is worth testing for configurable software delivery workflows and detailed issue reporting. Asana is better suited to cross-functional coordination across projects and departments. ClickUp may appeal to teams that want a broad configurable workspace, while Trello supports simpler Kanban-style work. Basecamp focuses on project communication and to-dos. These are different operating models, not interchangeable feature bundles; run the same sample workflow in each product before choosing.

sections.title: Selection Criteria
sections.body: Use the criteria below to compare options consistently.
items: Backlog, cycle or sprint planning, dependencies, and release traceability.
Reports that answer the questions engineering leads and stakeholders ask.
Required repository, chat, identity, and deployment integrations.
Permissions, guest access, audit history, and workflow administration.
Migration of issue history, labels, statuses, attachments, and relationships.
Current plan limits, onboarding, support, and long-term maintenance cost.

sections.title: Pilot Before Migrating
sections.body: Select one real project and test issue creation, triage, blocked work, ownership changes, planning, reporting, and export. Use the same tasks and scoring rubric for each candidate. Record where manual work remains and which settings require an administrator. Test migration on a small sample before moving active work. Keep the source system available until the team confirms that important records and relationships transferred correctly.

sections.title: Make the Decision
sections.body: Choose the alternative that supports the team's actual workflow with the fewest workarounds. A more configurable platform is not automatically better if nobody can maintain it; a simpler tool is not enough if it cannot represent critical dependencies or reporting. Record the trade-offs, plan assumptions, and unresolved questions so the decision can be reviewed at renewal.

selectionCriteria: Sprint or cycle planning and dependency visibility
